Forecast Discussion

High pressure is building in from the Midwest, but it is not here yet. A northwest wind keeps pushing a shallow layer of moisture up the west side of the mountains, so clouds are slow to leave, and a flurry is possible this morning. Clouds thin this evening as the wind dies.

The high settles over the central Appalachians by Tuesday and stays through Friday. That means sunshine, light wind, and afternoons that warm a little each day. Temperatures are above average for the second half of the week. Nights stay cold in valleys while the ridgetops turn milder.

The high slips toward the coast by the end of next weekend as a front approaches from the west. If we have any precipitation during the rest of November, it’s passing, light, and next week.
